subject: TritonBank — SOC 2 re-attestation sprint + seat & capacity uplift
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Verma <asha.verma@tritonbank.com>, procurement@tritonbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TritonBank — SOC 2 re-attestation sprint + seat & capacity uplift

Hi Asha / Triton procurement,

Quick summary: your SOC 2 re-attestation window is coming up in Q4 and you flagged both an expanded retention horizon and an increase in active seats (supporting fraud-detection vectors). We put together a proposed approach that minimizes disruption to your audit while giving you the temporary throughput to do a bulk evidence export and log snapshot.

Proposed plan (high level):
- Run a 3-wave re-attestation sprint across two weeks (evidence collection, QA, final handoff).
- Temporary Dedicated burst (2 weeks) to support evidence export and on-demand replay of audit traces.
- Retention carve: expand audit-log retention from 365 -> 540 days for the Triton tenant (rolling), with an option for an escrow snapshot at 720 days if the auditor requests full window coverage.
- Commercials: one-time seat uplift for the renewal quarter + a capped credit against the Dedicated burst usage (details in attached capacity-quote-8421.pdf).

Attachments: SOC2-Reattest-Checklist-2026.pdf (checklist + artifact list), evidence-wave-plan.xlsx (wave schedule), capacity-quote-8421.pdf (pricing + credit).

Can you confirm:
1) target attestation date (your auditor's preferred month),
2) who on your side will own evidence collection (security contact + backup), and
3) any special data residency or encryption requirements beyond what we already have documented?

If this looks good we can lock a MAP (mutual action plan) and route a short DocuSign amendment for the temporary burst and retention change.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Sr. Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

----
Attachment stubs:
- SOC2-Reattest-Checklist-2026.pdf (PDF, 28 pages)
- evidence-wave-plan.xlsx (Excel, 3 sheets)
- capacity-quote-8421.pdf (PDF, pricing)
From: Asha Verma <asha.verma@tritonbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tritonbank.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 14:30:45 -0400
Subject: Re: TritonBank — SOC 2 re-attestation sprint + seat & capacity uplift

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- Attestation timing: auditor is available mid-November for testing; we need artifact windows to be completed by end of October. Can you compress the sprint to finish evidence handoff by 2026-10-28?
- Retention: 540d is fine as an interim; auditor has asked us to show a 720d snapshot for a subset of critical audit streams (auth, admin, and payment routing). Can Redwood support an export/escrow snapshot for those streams?
- Logs: we will need a read-only export and a documented checksum/md5 manifest for every file the auditor receives. What is your delivery format?

Also, the security team requests an ISE (independent security engineer) walkthrough of your evidence staging area (S3 path and access controls). I'm copying procurement so they can queue the SOW amendment.

If we can get the compressed schedule and the escrow snapshot, we will proceed with the seat uplift.

Best,
Asha Verma
Head of Security Programs
TritonBank
asha.verma@tritonbank.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Verma <asha.verma@tritonbank.com>, procurement@tritonbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 08:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: TritonBank — SOC 2 re-attestation sprint + seat & capacity uplift

Hi Asha — thanks for the rapid follow. Short answers below and an updated ask list: 

Schedule: we can compress the 3-wave sprint into a 9-business-day run (evidence gathering starting 2026-10-14, handoff complete 2026-10-27). We will prioritize the auth/admin/payment routing artifact sets in wave 1 to meet your auditor's needs.

Escrow snapshot: yes — Redwood can produce a time-boxed archive (gzip tarball) of the three critical streams and provide an MD5 manifest for every file. Snapshot will be immutable and stored in your chosen escrow bucket for 90 days; longer retention is available as add-on.

Delivery format & access: S3-compatible export (presigned URLs for auditor read-only access) + signed manifest. If your auditor requires physical transfer, we can coordinate an encrypted tape export via partner courier (rare, but possible).

Security walkthrough: happy to schedule a 60-minute ISE session. Proposed attendees: Kimberly (security ops lead on our side), your ISE, and our infra engineer for the export. Please propose 2 preferred windows.

Commercials update: to enable the compressed timeline we will allocate Dedicated burst capacity for the 2-week export window. We can apply a one-time credit that offsets 40% of the burst fees if you commit to the seat uplift at renewal. Ben — please confirm the credit and finalize the amendment language for the DocuSign link.

Next steps:
- Asha: confirm auditor mid-November is acceptable and provide 2 windows for ISE walkthrough.
- Procurement: review capacity-quote-8421.pdf and the DocuSign amendment (link in original).
- Ben/Kimberly: confirm credit and legal redline timing.

Jonas

----
Note: evidence-wave-plan.xlsx updated (wave 1 prioritizes auth/admin/payment routing)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 12:18:33 -0700
Subject: Internal: TritonBank credit approval & legal redline

Ben — internal quick note so you have the context to close the amendment:

- I support the 40% burst credit for this renewal (strategic renewal + seat uplift). This buys us the compressed timeline and reduces operational churn.
- Ask Legal to prepare an amendment that:
  * adds temporary Dedicated burst window (2026-10-14 -> 2026-10-28) with capped spend,
  * modifies retention for Triton tenant to 540d rolling with an escrow snapshot clause for the named streams,
  * includes a one-time credit line that applies to the burst invoice when the renewal seats are confirmed.

Jonas — I will join the ISE walkthrough and own the export runbook.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Asha Verma <asha.verma@tritonbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tritonbank.com
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: TritonBank — SOC 2 re-attestation sprint + seat & capacity uplift

Thanks — that all looks good. Auditor availability is confirmed: Nov 15–20 for testing. We can do the ISE walkthrough on either Monday 2026-09-27 10:00–11:00 ET or Tuesday 2026-09-28 14:00–15:00 ET; prefer the 27th.

A couple of final asks before we sign: 
1) Please include a short statement of cryptographic controls for the escrowed tarball (algorithms, key management, and expiry).
2) Confirm that the MD5 manifest will be salted and signed, and provide the public key we can use to validate signatures.

Once we have those two items and DocuSign routing, procurement will execute the amendment and we'll confirm the seat uplift numbers.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looks like a clean path to renewal.

Regards,
Asha
